description.narrative:
Forest Governance the Urgency of the Moment, was a WWF project aiming to contribute to good governance in the forest sector by promoting participation and engagement of CSOs, the media and local communities and other key actors in a multi-stakeholder dialogue to improve the current status of forest governance in Mozambique. The project objective was to strengthen CSOs and local communities involvement in forest decision making and governance.
The project had 2 specific objectives (medium term outcomes):
Outcome 1. Civil society become key actors in influencing planning, decision-making and good governance of forest resources
Outcome 2. Communities increase influence in forest management decision making process and improve benefit sharing.
The project was implemented through the four CSO partners AAAJC, ADEL Sofala, Forum Terra Nampula and RADEZA.

Det fyra år långa projektet avsåg att stärka civilsamhällets tekniska kapacitet att driva påverkansarbete och utkräva ansvar för och förändring av styrningen av skogssektorn, samt att öka allmänhetens kunskap om de miljömässiga och ekonomiska konsekvenserna av den rådande situationen i Moçambiques skogssektor. För att uppnå detta engagerades såväl lokalbefolkningar som civilsamhällesorganisationer, media, privat sektor och offentliga institutioner i mediakampanjer, utbildningar och tvärsektoriell dialog angående skogssektorn. Projektet var nationellt, men med särskilt fokus på de provinser som är rikast på produktiv skog och/eller hårdast drabbade av illegal skogsskövling, nämligen Sofala, Zambézia, Tete, Nampula och Cabo Delgado.

The four-year long project aimed to strengthen the technical capacity of civil society to engage in advocacy, accountability and governance change in the forest sector, and to raise public awareness of the environmental and economic consequences of the current situation in the Mozambique forest sector. To achieve this, local populations as well as civil society organisations, the media, the private sector and public institutions were involved in media campaigns, training and cross-sectoral dialogue on the forest sector. The project was national, but with a particular focus on the provinces richest in productive forests and/or most affected by illegal deforestation, namely Sofala, Zambézia, Tete, Nampula and Cabo Delgado.

Examples of results reported during the last two years (2018-2019) of implementation:
- the training with the Attorney General offices from different districts on sustainable forest management and legislation has contributed to increased numbers of illegal logging cases prosecuted by the Attorney General (from less than five in FY 2018 to 50 in FY 2019).
- WWF in partnership with the Ministry of Land environment and Rural Development, National Directorate of Forestry (MITADER/DINAF) and the World Bank conducted the second assessment of forest operators (2018). The role of WWF was to ensure participation of CSOs in the process. It was then expected that more forest operators would be removed from the system as result of their poor performance.
- The Consolidation of Forest Governance Pilot Assessment in the province of Zambézia and Cabo Delgado (partnership with the World Bank and Eduardo Mondlane University): the results showed that in general the situation is far from desired, with critical forest governance in the country and a clear indication that the country is still far from having improved mechanism for forest governance.
- More than 35 news articles and reports on forest governance related topics and issues were produced and published by various media organizations. Most of these media products was a result of deep investigative activities conducted by the journalist group created under this project called FOJOCOM meaning Journalist Forum for Biodiversity Conservation in Mozambique.
- As a result of media intervention, 7 foreign citizen were detained due to illegal logging in the buffer zone of the Gorongosa National park and with a seizure of 20 m3 of timber and issued fines of about 9 million Meticais. Legal actions also led to offenders being sentenced from 2 to 14 years in prison (sentences appealed at the time of reporting).
- 30 committees from local communities were revitalized and trained in sustainable forest management (SFM) and forest legislation with participation of more than 200 community members (65% male and 35% female).
- Training manuals were produced in partnership with Eduardo Mondlane University and made available to partners to use as their guidebooks in SFM trainings.
- A multi-sectoral dialogue on SFM was started by WWF in partnership with IUCN, and the government, judiciary and civil society set up regular platforms to discuss how to improve forest governance in Mozambique.
- The National Forest Forum (FNF) of Civil Society Organisations was revitalized with WWF financial and technical support.
- WWF, representing the civil society, participated in the governmental consultation processes for reforms in forestry policy and the national Forestry Programme for the period 2018-2035.
- A new information and technology tool introduced for timber monitoring and tracking by CSOs and local communities, called TIMBY, was put to use by CSOs and Media to report all legal and illegal activities in the areas where forest harvesting is taking place, as well as along the roads and control posts.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
